Rich detailed gouache, warm colors, recognizable gentle expressions, full faces and hands. No text, watermarks, invented legible inscriptions or speech bubbles. In a modern museum gallery, the friends and their familiar teal-clad adult guide observe an UNLIT Changxin Palace lantern sculpture in a glass exhibit case. Depict a gold-bronze kneeling palace attendant holding a lamp basin, her broad right sleeve curving above the basin to connect it with the hollow figure. The true lantern design is the subject, do not create an electric lamp. The sculpture occupies the right half on a pedestal, with complete silhouette; friends on left point toward the lamp basin and curving sleeve without touching glass or artifact. In the foreground is a separate simple teaching display with a warm fan of projected light on a neutral card, not fire. Calm polished gallery. No active flames, no children lighting or dismantling anything. No fake inscriptions.

The friends and adult guide sit in a quiet Chinese museum reading area, studying how old history books keep different people's stories. An antique book is protected in a glass case in the BACKGROUND. On the FOREGROUND TABLE are two distinct large modern picture cards: LEFT shows a simplified thoughtful older teacher in a robe talking with pupils, RIGHT shows a simplified Qin ruler in a dark ceremonial robe with attendants, all small symbolic illustrations rather than claimed portraits. No written words on cards. Yellow boy studies the teacher card, girl points to the ruler card, green boy opens a modern notebook for recording. The three friends and teal guide safely observe an imagined scene from a classical poem, from a shore with a low wooden railing in the LEFT foreground. A small wooden rowing boat with two adult women in simple historical Chinese robes is in the CENTER LEFT among pink lotus flowers, reeds and green lotus leaves at evening, one woman holding an oar. On the RIGHT above a reed-covered sandbank, a SMALL FLOCK of white water birds has just risen into flight; wings are clear and distinct from lotus leaves. Lower-right shows calm shallow water and resting reed stems. Warm late sunset, lively but peaceful surprise, painterly lyrical scene. Clearly separate the boat from the birds so a child can point at either. The poet's outing is a literary imagination, not a verified portrait of Li Qingzhao; no wine, modern life scenes, dangerous overturned boat, or child at the oars.

In a safe Chinese garden art workshop, the three friends and teal guide explore how a bamboo plant can appear in both a painting and a poem. On the RIGHT stands a large real-looking living clump of slender green bamboo next to a rough garden rock; leaves bend gently with a breeze but stalks remain upright. On the LEFT foreground table is a clearly NEW children's ink painting of bamboo and rock on white paper, plain with no calligraphy. The yellow boy uses an open palm to feel the breeze, girl points between painted bamboo and living bamboo, green boy compares the rock shape while holding a soft brush above paper. Warm early morning light, clean spacious composition with bamboo and rock easily identifiable; no exact reproduction of Zheng Xie's real painting, no historical portrait, no glowing powers, no snapped bamboo or distress.
